info.title: Elmo API
info.description:
Read and manage the brands, prompts, competitors, and AI-visibility analytics of an Elmo deployment.

## Authentication

Every request carries a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Two kinds of token are accepted.

**Instance admin keys** come from the operator's `ADMIN_API_KEYS` environment variable. They reach every organization and every endpoint, including the admin-only ones, and are not subject to plan limits or rate limits.

**Organization keys** (`elmo_…`) are issued from the dashboard. A key acts inside exactly one organization, carries an explicit set of scopes, and may be narrowed further to a subset of that organization's brands. Plan limits, read-only mode, and per-key rate limits all apply.

## Scopes

Each operation lists the scope it requires in `x-elmo-scopes`. Admin keys hold every scope implicitly.

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `brands:read` / `brands:write` | Read or manage brands |
| `prompts:read` / `prompts:write` / `prompts:delete` | Read, manage, or delete prompts |
| `competitors:read` / `competitors:write` / `competitors:delete` | Read, manage, or delete competitors |
| `analytics:read` | Read aggregated visibility, share of voice, citations, and fan-out |
| `runs:read` | Read individual model answers and their citations |
| `billing:read` | Read the organization's plan, limits, and usage |

Deleting is a scope of its own wherever a delete exists: removing a prompt takes its runs and citations with it, and an integration that syncs prompts has no business erasing history.

There is deliberately no billing write scope: the API cannot change a subscription, an add-on quantity, or a payment method under any key, including an admin key. Operations marked `x-elmo-admin-only` — report generation and brand analysis — are reachable with an instance admin key only; no scope grants them, because both spend provider budget with no organization to bill it to.

## Access and errors

A brand outside the calling key's reach answers `404` with the same body a brand that does not exist would, so a key can never probe another tenant's data. A key that is valid but lacks the scope an operation requires answers `403` naming the missing scope.

Errors share one envelope — `{ error, message, code }` — where `code` is a stable machine-readable string. Treat an unrecognized `code` as its HTTP status implies; new values are added without a version bump.

## Conventions

Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC; dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Lists take `page` (1-based) and `limit` (max 100) and answer with a `pagination` object. Analytics endpoints take either `startDate` + `endDate` (with an optional `timezone`) or the `lookback` shorthand — one form or the other, never both.

## Stability

Every operation carries `x-elmo-stability`, and any operation that isn't `stable` says so in the first line of its description.

- `stable` — the response shape will only ever gain fields.
- `beta` — built and supported, but the shape may still change: we may add, rename, or remove a response field, and we'll say so in the release that does it. Pin nothing you can't adjust.
- `planned` — specified here, not built yet. Calling it returns `404`. This document is written ahead of the code, so the reference doubles as the roadmap.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Deliberately not an enum: new values are added without a version bump, so treat an unrecognized one as its HTTP status implies. Currently: `unauthorized`, `insufficient_scope`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `validation_error`, `conflict`, `rate_limited`, `read_only`, `no_active_plan`, `brand_limit`, `prompt_limit`, `platform_not_in_plan`, `platform_picks_exceeded`, `premium_not_in_plan`, `premium_pool_exhausted`, `cadence_faster_than_plan`, `system_tag_immutable`, `internal_error`.

brandWebsite.description: The brand's website — a domain (nike.com) or a full URL. A URL with a path (e.g. https://www.nike.com/golf) scopes the analysis to that page; mentions are tracked against its domain either way.

manualPrompts.description: Optional list of custom prompts to include in the report

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the report was created

ReportPromptSnapshot.description: Per-prompt snapshot of raw mention data from a report. Consumers compute SoV and other derived metrics.

promptValue.description: The prompt text that was evaluated

totalRuns.description: Number of evaluation runs for this prompt

MentionsSummary.description: Aggregated mention counts for a prompt across its evaluation runs.

mentionsTotal.description: Total brand + competitor mentions across all runs

brandMentionsTotal.description: Number of runs where the brand was mentioned

competitorMentionsTotal.description: Total count of individual competitor mentions across all runs (a single run mentioning 3 competitors counts as 3)

mentionsTopK.description: Top-K competitor entities ranked by mention count

count.description: Number of runs where this entity was mentioned
Number of times this URL was cited

website.description: Brand's website — a hostname or a full URL. A URL with a path (e.g. https://www.nike.com/golf) is analyzed as given; the returned website is always its domain.

brandName.description: Optional brand name hint. If omitted, inferred from the domain.

maxCompetitors.description: Maximum number of competitor suggestions. 0 disables competitor generation entirely.

maxPrompts.description: Maximum number of suggested prompts. 0 disables prompt generation entirely.

CreateBrandRequest.description: Create a brand. Skips onboarding. The first entry in `domains` is treated as the brand's primary website; the rest are stored as additional domains.

domains.description: Brand domains. The first entry is the primary website; remaining entries are additional domains.

organizationId.description: Workspace to create the brand in. Admin keys only, and optional: omitted, an admin key provisions a new organization named after the brand id, exactly as it does today. Ignored for organization keys, which always create inside their own.

UpdateBrandRequest.description: Update brand-level fields. At least one field must be provided. Provided arrays replace the stored values verbatim. When `domains` is provided, the first entry becomes the primary website and the rest become additional domains. Prompts and competitors are managed via /prompts and /competitors.

organizationId.description: The workspace that owns this brand and is billed for it.

enabledModels.description: Platforms this brand is tracked on. Null means the deployment default.

delayOverrideHours.description: Sampling cadence override in hours. Null means the plan cadence.

CreateCompetitorRequest.description: Add a competitor to a brand.

UpdateCompetitorRequest.description: Update a competitor. At least one field must be provided. Provided arrays replace the stored values verbatim.

brandId.description: Brand identifier this prompt belongs to

endDate.description: End of the queried date range (YYYY-MM-DD)

brandCitationsTotal.description: Number of citations to brand-owned domains

competitorCitationsTotal.description: Number of citations to competitor-owned domains

citedUrlsTopK.description: Top-K cited URLs ranked by frequency

DateRange.description: The window the response was computed over, resolved from either the explicit dates or the lookback shorthand.

keyType.description: `admin` for an instance key, `organization` for a dashboard-issued key.

organizationId.description: The organization this key acts inside. Null for admin keys.

scopes.description: Scopes this key holds. Admin keys list every scope.

brandIds.description: Brands the key is narrowed to, or null when it reaches every brand in its organization. Never an empty array — a restriction to no brands is rejected at creation rather than treated as no restriction.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working, if it has an expiry.

rateLimit.description: The key's configured limit. Enforcement is a fixed window and approximate under concurrency.

billingEnabled.description: Whether plan limits and the billing endpoints apply.

createdBy.description: Name of the member who issued the key. Null for admin keys.

id.description: Model identifier used by the `model` filter, e.g. `chatgpt`.

premiumCapable.description: Whether this platform can be tracked grounded, spending a premium pairing.

configured.description: Whether this deployment is actually wired to reach the platform.

PlanLimits.description: The organization's plan limits. Every field is null on deployments without billing.

maxPrompts.description: Enabled prompts across the whole organization. Null means no limit.

platformMenu.description: Platforms the plan may pick from. Null means any.

OrganizationBilling.description: Read-only view of an organization's subscription, limits, and usage. The API has no way to change any of it: there is no billing write endpoint and no billing write scope. Stripe identifiers, payment methods, and invoices are deliberately not exposed — those live in the Stripe customer portal.

billingEnabled.description: False on self-hosted deployments, where nothing is metered.

plan.description: Null when the organization has no subscription, or when billing is disabled.

key.description: Plan identifier, or `custom` for a negotiated plan.

standing.description: What the subscription means for service, and the only field a caller needs to act on: `active` and `grace` keep tracking running, `paused` stops it, `none` is unsubscribed. The payment provider's own status string is deliberately not passed through.

trackingActive.description: Whether prompts are currently being sampled.

BrandSummary.description: Every headline figure the dashboard shows for a brand, in one request.

visibility.description: Share of runs mentioning the brand at the end of the window. Percentage 0–100.

shareOfVoice.description: The brand's share of all brand and competitor mentions. Percentage 0–100.

totalPrompts.description: Enabled prompts counted in the window.

platforms.description: Platforms that produced at least one run in the window.

visibility.description: Null on days with no runs to plot; the series is not gap-filled with zeros. Percentage 0–100.

currentVisibility.description: The last plotted point — the number the dashboard hero shows. Percentage 0–100.

isBrand.description: True for the tracked brand's own row.

prompts.description: Distinct prompts this entity appeared in.

brandShare.description: The brand's own share at the end of the window. Percentage 0–100.

visibility.description: Share of this platform's runs that mentioned the brand. Percentage 0–100.

category.description: Which side of the citation landscape the domain sits on.

count.description: Citations to this domain in the window.

share.description: Share of all citations in the window. Percentage 0–100.

promptCount.description: Distinct prompts whose answers cited this domain.

previousCount.description: Citations in the equal-length window immediately before this one.

changePercent.description: Change against the previous window. Null when the domain is new.

category.description: Which side of the citation landscape the domain sits on.

pageType.description: What kind of page was cited.

isNew.description: Not cited in the equal-length window immediately before this one.

query.description: A search the engine ran while answering.

fanoutRuns.description: Runs that searched at all. Engines that don't expose their searches contribute runs but no queries.

coverageRate.description: Share of runs that searched. Percentage 0–100.

brandMentionRate.description: Share of this prompt's runs mentioning the brand. Percentage 0–100.

RunSummary.description: A single model answer, without its text. Fetch `GET /runs/{runId}` for the answer itself.

provider.description: How the answer was obtained. Informational; not a stable enum.

webSearchEnabled.description: Whether the engine answered with its own web search on.

webQueries.description: Searches the engine ran, where it exposes them.

citationIndex.description: Position within the answer's citation list.

Run.description: One model answer with its normalized text and citations.

text.description: The answer, normalized out of the provider's response. Null when nothing could be extracted.

BulkCreatePromptsRequest.description: All-or-nothing: the whole batch is checked against the plan as one delta and either every prompt is created or none is.

premiumModels.description: Platforms to track this prompt on grounded. Each entry spends one premium pairing.

name.description: The tag, normalized to lower case.

promptCount.description: Prompts in this brand carrying the tag.

system.description: True for `branded` and `unbranded`, which Elmo computes from the prompt text. A system tag always appears here; applying it to a prompt as a user tag overrides the computed classification rather than creating a new tag.

data.description: System tags first, then user tags alphabetically — the order the dashboard's filter shows.

RenameTagRequest.description: Renames the tag on every prompt in the brand that carries it. Merging into an existing tag is allowed and deduplicates.

name.description: The new tag. Normalized the same way tags on a prompt are.
The tag after the change, or null when it was removed.

promptsUpdated.description: Prompts whose tag list actually changed.

text.description: The prompt as the report names it.

promptId.description: The tracked prompt it resolved to, or null when it didn't match one.

category.description: Which workstream this belongs to: `creation` is net-new content, `existing-content` is a page that could win the mention with a refresh, `outreach` is earning a placement on a third-party site assistants cite, `social` is the community conversations they pull from.

title.description: Short and action-oriented — the concrete surface or angle.

why.description: Why it is worth doing, in plain language.

relatedPrompts.description: Tracked prompts this would help. May be empty.

yourCitations.description: Pages on the brand's own domains already cited for those prompts.

competitorCitations.description: Pages on competitor domains cited for those prompts.

BrandOpportunities.description: The brand's latest Opportunities report — the same LLM-generated analysis the dashboard shows, read from the append-only history rather than regenerated. Elmo decides when to produce a new one; there is no way to trigger generation over the API, because it spends provider budget with no per-call metering behind it.

status.description: `ready` when a report is present. `insufficient-data` when the brand hasn't accumulated enough tracked answers to say anything useful yet. `not-generated` when none has been produced for this brand at all. The lists are empty for anything but `ready`.

model.description: The model that produced the report, when recorded.

summary.description: A few bullets on where the brand stands and the through-line of the plan.

risks.description: Caveats: hard-to-win areas, or tactics to avoid.

ForbiddenError.description: The key is valid but not permitted: a missing scope, an admin-only endpoint, or a write in read-only (demo) mode.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window. Counted with a read-modify-write per request, so treat it as a guide and back off on 429 rather than riding it to zero.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix seconds at which the window resets.

PaymentRequiredError.description: The organization has no active subscription. Cloud deployments only.

get.description:
**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Domains the engines cited when answering this brand's prompts, categorized and compared against the equal-length window immediately before this one.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Individual pages the engines cited, with their category and page type.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

The brand's most recent Opportunities report: a prioritized set of ways to get cited more often, with the tracked prompts and cited pages behind each one. The same analysis the dashboard shows.

Read-only. Elmo generates a report when the brand's data has moved enough to warrant one; there is no way to trigger generation over the API, because it spends provider budget with nothing metering it per call. `status` says why the lists are empty when they are.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Runs, mentions, and visibility broken down by answer engine, so a customer can see where they are strong and where they are invisible.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Per-prompt mention rates over the window. The analytics counterpart to `GET /prompts?brandId=`, which returns prompt configuration rather than results.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

The searches engines ran while answering this brand's prompts. Engines that don't expose their searches still contribute runs, so `coverageRate` is the honest denominator.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

The brand against its tracked competitors: a leaderboard of mention counts and shares, plus the brand's own share over time.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Every headline figure the dashboard shows for a brand — visibility, share of voice, and period totals — in a single request.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Every tag in use on the brand's prompts, with how many carry each — enough to build the same filter the dashboard shows without paging the whole prompt list to derive it.

Tags are not a resource of their own: a tag exists exactly as long as some prompt carries it. `branded` and `unbranded` are computed by Elmo and always listed.

patch.description:
**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Rename the tag on every prompt in the brand that carries it. Renaming onto a tag that already exists merges the two and deduplicates.

Needs `prompts:write`, not `prompts:delete`: this relabels prompts and destroys no tracked data, and a caller holding `prompts:write` could already do it one `PATCH /prompts/{promptId}` at a time.

The computed `branded` and `unbranded` tags cannot be renamed (`409 system_tag_immutable`).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: The tag, matched case-insensitively.

delete.description:
**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

Remove the tag from every prompt in the brand that carries it. The prompts themselves, and their runs and citations, are untouched — which is why this needs `prompts:write` rather than `prompts:delete`.

The computed `branded` and `unbranded` tags cannot be removed (`409 system_tag_immutable`).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: The tag, matched case-insensitively.

get.description:
**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

A daily series of the share of runs that mentioned the brand, plus period totals. Days with no runs to plot carry `null` rather than zero, so a gap in sampling never reads as a collapse in visibility.

get.description:
**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

What this key is, which organization and brands it reaches, which scopes it holds, and what kind of deployment answered. Requires no scope, so it is always safe to call first when wiring up an integration.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

One entry for an organization key — the one it acts inside. Every organization for an instance admin key. No scope required: a key can only ever see the workspace it is already bound to.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

No scope required. An organization outside the key's reach answers `404`, identically to one that does not exist.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

The organization's plan, its limits, and how much of each limit is already spent — enough for an integration to know a write will be rejected before attempting it.

This endpoint is read-only by construction. No API key of any kind can change a subscription, an add-on quantity, or a payment method; there is no billing write endpoint and no billing write scope. Stripe identifiers, invoices, and payment methods are never returned.

Deployments without billing answer `200` with `billingEnabled: false`, a null plan, and null limits, so callers need no special case.

**Beta — supported, but the response shape may still change.**

The answer engines this deployment can track, with the identifiers accepted by every `model` filter. Lets a client build a platform picker without hardcoding names.

Create a new AI Share of Voice report and queue it for generation. The report will evaluate the brand across multiple AI engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Google AI) using generated and optional custom prompts.

Requires an instance admin key; organization keys receive `403`.
